skill.summary: Configure a branded WordPress admin experience with free white-label plugins and WP-CLI automation.
skill.author: CrazySwami

security_audit.summary: Most Markdown backtick and hardcoded URL findings are documentation false positives. Confirmed risk remains in Bash and WP-CLI automation, fixed /tmp handoff files, raw HTML/CSS option writes, and configurable remote media downloads.

remediation.suggestion: Allow only approved http or https hosts, reject private network addresses, and require confirmation before fetching external media.

remediation.issue: Stored HTML and CSS from configuration
remediation.suggestion: Sanitize welcome HTML and custom CSS, restrict allowed tags and attributes, and escape values before writing plugin options.

remediation.issue: Fixed /tmp handoff and privileged WP-CLI execution
remediation.suggestion: Use unique temporary filenames with restrictive permissions, verify file hashes before eval-file, and avoid --allow-root unless required.

remediation.issue: Automation commands can affect live sites
remediation.suggestion: Add a dry-run mode and require explicit target site or container confirmation before Bash, Docker, or WP-CLI commands.

semantic_findings.title: Unvalidated HTML and CSS Written to WordPress Options
semantic_findings.description: The WP-CLI script writes config-provided dashboard HTML and custom CSS into plugin options. If a config is generated from untrusted input, this can create stored admin content injection.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Lines 180-193 and 310 assign raw config values to WordPress options, and the example config uses HTML in welcome_message. The risk depends on configuration trust.

semantic_findings.title: Configurable Remote Media Download
semantic_findings.description: The script can fetch a logo from a config-provided URL and sideload it into WordPress. Without URL allowlists or private-network checks, this can contact attacker-controlled or internal endpoints.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code directly passes logo_url to download_url, and the documentation encourages URL-based logo configuration. WordPress may apply some URL safety checks, so confidence is medium.

content.value_statement: Agencies often need branded WordPress admin areas without paid plugins or manual drift. This skill guides setup and automation for login branding, dashboard cleanup, menus, and handoff checks.
actual_capabilities: Plans white-label setup with ASE, White Label CMS, Branda, and Admin Menu Editor.
Provides WP-CLI automation for login branding, dashboard widgets, admin footer, and security options.
Uses a JSON configuration file for company name, logo, colors, login slug, menus, and dashboard text.
Supports local WP-CLI execution and Docker container execution.
Includes troubleshooting steps for login URLs, logos, admin bar items, and saved settings.
Supplies a client handoff checklist for branding, security, and admin cleanup.
limitations: Requires WordPress administrator access and installed free plugins.
Automation can change live site options and should run only after confirmation.
Plugin option names may change across plugin versions.
Remote logos, custom HTML, and custom CSS must come from trusted sources.

use_cases.title: Brand a Client Site
use_cases.description: Apply agency or client branding to the WordPress login page, admin footer, dashboard, and menu labels.

use_cases.title: Prepare Client Handoff
use_cases.description: Clean up advanced admin screens, verify branded elements, and produce a practical handoff checklist.

use_cases.title: Standardize Reusable Setups
use_cases.description: Create a repeatable configuration flow for multiple WordPress projects using free plugins and WP-CLI.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a White-Label Setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to plan a WordPress white-label setup for [Company]. Include login branding, dashboard cleanup, menus, and security checks.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Brand Settings
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare white-label settings for [Company] with logo URL [URL], primary color [color], and login slug [slug]. Explain each setting first.

prompt_templates.title: Apply a Staged Setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my WordPress container [container] and config file [path]. Confirm the target, then apply the white-label script and summarize changes.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Client Handoff
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect the completed white-label setup for [site]. Verify plugin settings, hidden menus, login URL, XML-RPC, author slugs, and handoff risks.

output_examples.input: White-label a new client site for Acme Studio.
output: Recommends ASE for login security, White Label CMS for dashboard branding, and Branda for login styling.
Lists required brand assets, colors, login slug, dashboard text, and menu changes before applying settings.
Requests confirmation before running WP-CLI or Docker commands against the target site.

output_examples.input: Prepare handoff after applying the branding.
output_examples.output: Produces a checklist covering login URL tests, logo checks, hidden menu review, dashboard cleanup, and plugin setting verification.

output_examples.input: Troubleshoot why the branded login logo is missing.
output_examples.output: Checks image dimensions, media URL accessibility, cache state, Branda settings, and possible plugin conflicts.

best_practices: Back up the site and database before applying white-label automation.
Confirm the exact WordPress site, Docker container, and configuration file before running commands.
Sanitize remote media URLs, dashboard HTML, and custom CSS before saving plugin options.
anti_patterns: Do not run the automation script against production without a backup and explicit confirmation.
Do not use untrusted logo URLs, dashboard HTML, or custom CSS in the configuration file.
Do not hide admin menus that site maintainers need for security, updates, or recovery.

faq.question: Does this skill require paid plugins?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on free plugins, including ASE, White Label CMS, Branda, and optional Admin Menu Editor.

faq.question: Can it run against Docker-based WordPress sites?
faq.answer: Yes. The included shell script supports a Docker container target when WP-CLI is available inside the container.

faq.question: Can it run on a local WordPress installation?
faq.answer: Yes. It can use local WP-CLI when no Docker container argument is provided.

faq.question: Does it change security settings?
faq.answer: Yes. It can configure login URL changes, XML-RPC disabling, author slug obfuscation, and email obfuscation.

faq.question: What should be reviewed before running automation?
faq.answer: Review the target site, config file, logo URL, custom HTML, custom CSS, and backup status.

faq.question: Is the automation safe for untrusted configuration files?
faq.answer: No. Treat configuration files as trusted admin input because they can affect branding, HTML, CSS, and site options.
